comparator.name: Media and Culture
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 public curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official English curriculum supplies 60 EC in each year. Year 1 is a shared media-studies foundation. Year 2 includes three 12-EC restricted-choice groups in which students choose Film Studies or Television and Cross-Media Culture, alongside Global Media Culture, Media Worlds and two philosophy courses. The normalized target names neither route, so the first-listed Film Studies route is selected consistently across all three groups under the neutral official-order rule. Year 3 contains 42 EC of genuine free choice and an 18-EC research seminar and bachelor thesis.

alternatives.label: Media, film & cultural analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates film and media, literature, visual culture, history, sociology, philosophy and research across a broad cultural-analysis pathway.
alternatives.concept: A broad response to Media and Culture that combines film and media analysis with narrative, art history, heritage, cultural theory, sociology, philosophy, criticism and independent historical research.
progression: Introductions to visual culture, literature, film, history and sociology precede advanced film-and-text analysis, media and race, museums, social theory, creative communication and independent historical research. All formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Film, visual storytelling & archives
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates on film, documentary, adaptation, images, museums, heritage, narrative and visual communication.
alternatives.concept: Develops the official Film direction through film and documentary analysis, literature and adaptation, visual storytelling, art history, museums, heritage, philosophy and creative communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, seven courses replace broad art-history, sociology, social theory and historical-research coverage with rhetoric, archaeology, environmental media, philosophy and persuasive communication. The 52.5-EC change yields a screen-, narrative- and communication-centred Film pathway.
progression: Foundations in film and media, literature, rhetoric, archaeology, history and philosophy precede documentary, adaptation, environmental media, advanced film-and-text work, media and race, museums and creative communication. Verified offerings and all formal prerequisites are respected; seven courses are level 3.

alternatives.label: Television, audiences & cross-media culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum connects audiovisual analysis and communication with audiences, social research, identity, organisations, platforms and cross-media practice.
alternatives.concept: Develops the Television and Cross-Media Culture direction through audiovisual analysis, rhetoric, audiences, empirical methods, sociology, identity, organisations, persuasive communication and creative media practice.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, fourteen courses move away from broad art history, heritage, literary survey and historical research toward rhetoric, audience methods, environmental and cross-media analysis, organisational psychology, leadership, market research and social theory. Fifteen courses differ from the Film alternative, well above the pairwise floor.
progression: Introductory media, rhetoric, sociology and research methods precede documentary and environmental media, audience research, social theory, persuasive and creative communication, organisational leadership, market research and philosophy. Every course is in a verified offering, formal prerequisites are met and eight courses are level 3.

selection.assessment: Three feasible and materially distinct UCR curricula are included: a broad closest match, a Film-led direction and a Television and Cross-Media direction. These cover the official programme structure and stable study directions at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated Media Studies sequence with explicit Film and Television practice choices. UCR combines related media, communication, literature, visual culture, history, philosophy and social-science courses but does not reproduce UvA production facilities or its compulsory 12-EC practice blocks. The comparison therefore reflects academic direction rather than one-to-one professional production equivalence.
